Hence $\\pi(T)\\in S_\\infty$","note":"T may be infinite, so pi(T) is undefined; the required self-duality and hence finiteness are not proved."},"L6.3":{"established":"yes","quote":"Let $T:=\\#\\bigl(S_\\infty\\cap[a_1,a_1+L)\\bigr)$... Writing $n=jT+r$: $a_{n+T}=a_{(j+1)T+r}=a_r+(j+1)L=a_n+L$ for every $n\\ge1$.","note":"Given finitely many minimal elements, Step 2 correctly proves periodicity from the first term."}},"S_ref":1,"notes":"The characterization and conditional periodicity assembly are valid. The finiteness argument fails because an inclusion-minimal transversal of an intersecting family of finite sets need not be finite, yet Claim 3.2 applies pi(T) without proving finiteness."}
